chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Isma'il al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from a man, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is sufficient disgrace for a person that he wears clothing by which he is defamed, or rides an animal which defames him.

key_terms.ثَوْب: Garment, clothing — used broadly for any article of dress
key_terms.خِزْي: Disgrace, humiliation, shame — a strong term implying public dishonor
key_terms.دَابَّة: Animal, mount — any riding beast; here connoting an ostentatious or attention-drawing mount
key_terms.يَشْهَرُهُ: Defames/makes notorious — from shuhrah, fame or notoriety through conspicuous display

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about wearing conspicuous clothing or riding a defaming animal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against seeking attention through ostentation in dress or mount, considering such behavior a form of self-inflicted disgrace. This teaching addresses the Islamic virtue of modesty (tawadu') and discourages the pursuit of shuhrah (notoriety/fame through conspicuous display). In early Islamic society, one's clothing and mount were powerful social signals; wearing extravagant or attention-seeking attire was considered a mark of vanity contrary to the Prophet's example of simplicity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, form Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Abu Ismail Al Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is sufficient disgrace for the man that he wears clothes by which he is defamed, or rides an animal which defames him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from abu ’Isma‘il al-Sarraj from ibn Muskan from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is enough humiliation for a man to wear a dress that causes public abhorrence or use such a stumper.’”
